dataset.name: JaGOOD MVP Commodity Profiles
dataset.purpose: Provide commodity inputs for route-risk inference and scenario simulation.
dataset.preprocessing: temp_ideal_min_c, temp_ideal_max_c, and shelf_life_hours_at_ideal_temp were cross-checked on 2026-08-22/23 against public food-safety guidance (FDA, USDA/USDA FSIS, UC Davis Postharvest Research Center, IDFA, and one commercial produce reference for a commodity with no government/academic source); several values were corrected or set to match cited guidance. delay_tolerance_hours and temp_sensitivity_level have almost no equivalent in public consumer/food-safety literature -- those sources mostly describe safe storage duration under ideal refrigeration, not tolerance to in-transit temperature/time deviation. Two categories of exception were found and applied where they exist: FDA's explicit cut-melon 4-hour room-temperature-abuse limit, and USDA's general dairy/egg 2-hour room-temperature rule -- both used for delay_tolerance_hours on the specific commodities they cover. Values are loaded without numerical transformation.
limitations: temp_ideal_min_c, temp_ideal_max_c, and shelf_life_hours_at_ideal_temp are grounded in cited public food-safety guidance, but that guidance targets consumer/commercial refrigeration safety, not cold-chain logistics specifically -- treat them as reasonable proxies, not regulatory transport standards.

delay_tolerance_hours and temp_sensitivity_level are internal MVP judgment calls for most commodities; only Semangka Potong, Telur Ayam Segar, Keju Segar, and Yogurt have a delay_tolerance_hours value matching a direct public citation (FDA cut-melon rule / USDA 2-hour dairy-and-egg rule) -- the field's overall classification stays DEMO since the current schema has no per-record field override and most commodities still lack any citation for it.

Kangkung Segar and Wortel Segar rely on a commercial industry reference and a partial citation (freezing-injury threshold only, no explicit shelf-life duration found) respectively -- weaker-tier grounding than the FDA/USDA/UC Davis sources used elsewhere, called out explicitly in their source notes.

Tomat Segar's ideal temperature (10-13C) is intentionally warmer than every other commodity in this dataset -- tomatoes are chilling-sensitive and develop quality defects when refrigerated near 0-4C like most other items here; this is a genuine horticultural distinction, not an error.

Values have not been validated against actual Indonesian cold-chain shipment outcomes; see app/services/historical_baseline.py and the shipment_records/corridor_baseline_stats tables for how real outcome data is (separately) collected going forward.
Shelf life and delay tolerance are simplified model inputs and must not be presented as guaranteed remaining product life or a food-safety certification.

sources.title: JaGOOD hackathon MVP commodity assumptions
sources.publisher: JaGOOD project team
sources.notes: Internal manually curated assumptions for commodity_type selection and for delay_tolerance_hours/temp_sensitivity_level on commodities with no public literature equivalent.

sources.title: Selecting and Serving Fresh and Frozen Seafood Safely
sources.publisher: U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA)
sources.notes: Fresh fish/seafood: store at 40F (4C) or below, use within 2 days of purchase. Applied to Salmon Segar, Udang Segar, Tuna Segar, and -- as the closest available general-seafood guidance -- Kepiting Segar and Cumi-cumi Segar (no crab- or squid-specific FDA/USDA storage guidance found).

sources.title: Frozen seafood storage guidance (0F/-18C indefinite safety; 6-12 month best-quality window)
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA)
sources.notes: Applied to Udang Beku.

sources.title: The Poultry Label Says "Fresh"
sources.publisher: USDA Food Safety and Inspection Service (FSIS)
sources.notes: Fresh raw poultry: 40F (4C) or below, use within 1-2 days. Applied to Ayam Segar.

sources.title: Chicken from Farm to Table
sources.publisher: USDA Food Safety and Inspection Service (FSIS)
sources.notes: Frozen at 0F (-18C) is safe indefinitely; best quality within about 1 year for whole poultry. This dataset uses the more conservative ~180-day figure (matching Udang Beku's convention) rather than the full 1-year best-quality window. Applied to Daging Ayam Beku.

sources.title: Ground Beef and Food Safety
sources.publisher: USDA Food Safety and Inspection Service (FSIS)
sources.notes: Whole-muscle fresh beef cuts: 3-5 days at 40F (4C) or below (ground beef only 1-2 days -- this dataset models whole-cut beef). Applied to Daging Sapi Segar.

sources.title: Pasteurized milk refrigeration guidance
sources.publisher: U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) / U.S. Dairy
sources.notes: Ideal storage 34-38F (1-3C), FDA ceiling 45F; 5-7 days at or below 40F. Applied to Susu Segar.

sources.title: How long can you keep dairy products like yogurt, milk, and cheese in the refrigerator? / general dairy 2-hour room-temperature rule
sources.publisher: USDA Food Safety and Inspection Service (FSIS) / U.S. Dairy
sources.license: U.S. Government / publicly available industry guidance
sources.notes: Soft cheese: ~1 week refrigerated. Yogurt: 1-2 weeks refrigerated (this dataset uses the conservative 1-week end). Dairy generally should not sit at room temperature more than 2 hours -- that figure is applied to delay_tolerance_hours for Keju Segar and Yogurt specifically, the same way FDA's cut-melon rule is applied to Semangka Potong. Applied to Keju Segar, Yogurt.

sources.title: Shell Eggs from Farm to Table
sources.publisher: USDA Food Safety and Inspection Service (FSIS)
sources.notes: Refrigerate at 40F (4C) or below; raw shell eggs keep 3-5 weeks refrigerated (this dataset uses the conservative 3-week/21-day end). USDA also states refrigerated eggs should not sit out more than 2 hours -- applied to delay_tolerance_hours for Telur Ayam Segar, the same pattern as the melon and dairy exceptions above. Applied to Telur Ayam Segar.

sources.title: Spinach produce facts sheet
sources.publisher: UC Davis Postharvest Research and Extension Center
sources.notes: Spinach: 3-5 days refrigerated at 0C. Applied to Bayam Segar.

sources.title: Water Spinach Information and Facts
sources.publisher: Specialty Produce (commercial produce industry reference, not a government or academic body)
sources.notes: Unwashed water spinach: 1-3 days refrigerated (up to 5 days with careful handling). Weaker-tier source than FDA/USDA/UC Davis -- no government or academic postharvest study found specifically for Ipomoea aquatica as of this research pass. Applied to Kangkung Segar; conservative low end (2 days) used for shelf_life_hours_at_ideal_temp.

sources.title: Bok Choy (Pak Choi, Pok Choi) produce facts sheet
sources.publisher: UC Davis Postharvest Research and Extension Center
sources.notes: Bok choy (closest documented analog to Indonesian sawi/pakcoy) stored at 0C can keep up to 40 days -- materially more robust than spinach/water spinach; higher temperatures accelerate yellowing, water loss, and decay. Applied to Sawi Segar.

sources.title: Carrot produce facts sheet
sources.publisher: UC Davis Postharvest Research and Extension Center
sources.notes: Freezing injury occurs at -1.2C (29.5F) or lower -- used only to ground the lower storage-temperature bound. No explicit multi-week shelf-life figure was found in this research pass; shelf_life_hours_at_ideal_temp for Wortel Segar (14 days) is therefore a conservative internal estimate, not a direct citation -- weaker grounding than the temperature bound. Applied to Wortel Segar.

sources.title: Tomato produce facts sheet
sources.publisher: UC Davis Postharvest Research and Extension Center
sources.notes: Tomatoes are chilling-sensitive: injury develops below 10C if held over 2 weeks, or below 5C if held over 6-8 days -- unlike every other commodity in this dataset, tomatoes should NOT be refrigerated near 0-4C. temp_ideal_min/max_c (10-13C) and shelf_life_hours_at_ideal_temp (14 days, the point chilling injury risk begins at the coldest safe temperature) reflect this directly. Applied to Tomat Segar.

sources.title: Commodity Specific Food Safety Guidelines for the Melon Supply Chain
sources.publisher: U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA)
sources.notes: Cut melon: store at 0-5C (32-41F); date-marked and used within 7 days; discard after 4 hours if held above 41F or product temperature exceeds 70F. The 4-hour figure is also applied to delay_tolerance_hours for Semangka Potong specifically -- one of four commodities in this dataset where that field has a direct public citation rather than being an internal DEMO estimate (see field_provenance note).

sources.title: Tips on Storing & Handling Ice Cream
sources.publisher: International Dairy Foods Association (IDFA)
sources.notes: 0F (-18C) or colder; best quality 2-4 months. Applied to Es Krim.

sources.title: Guide to Minimize Food Safety Hazards of Fresh-cut Produce
sources.publisher: U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA)
sources.notes: Fresh-cut produce held at or below 41F (5C); shelf life 7-20 days across produce types, though the 7-day figure documented there is specifically for melons/tomatoes/leafy greens -- browning-prone cut fruit (e.g. mango, papaya, pineapple) is not explicitly covered, so this dataset keeps a conservative shelf-life estimate rather than the upper end of that range. Applied to Mangga Potong, Pepaya Potong, and Nanas Potong.

sources.title: Freezing and Food Safety
sources.publisher: USDA Food Safety and Inspection Service (FSIS)
sources.notes: Frozen at 0F (-18C) or below is safe indefinitely; best quality for steaks/roasts is 4-12 months. This dataset uses a conservative ~180-day figure (matching the Beku convention used elsewhere) rather than the upper end. Applied to Daging Sapi Beku.

sources.title: Potato (Early Crop) produce facts sheet
sources.publisher: UC Davis Postharvest Research and Extension Center
sources.notes: Storage near 0C for a few weeks can cause chilling-injury discoloration (mahogany internal tissue) in some varieties -- this dataset uses a moderate 4-10C range instead of near-0C to avoid that, based on this qualitative description rather than an explicit stated ideal range. No exact multi-week shelf-life duration was found in this research pass; the 14-day figure is a conservative internal estimate, weaker grounding than the temperature guidance. Applied to Kentang Segar.

sources.title: Broccoli produce facts sheet
sources.publisher: UC Davis Postharvest Research and Extension Center
sources.notes: At 0C, storage life is at least 1 month (720h); at 5C it drops to ~14 days, and at 10C to ~5 days -- storage life is highly temperature-sensitive. Applied to Brokoli Segar.

sources.title: Mushroom produce facts sheet
sources.publisher: UC Davis Postharvest Research and Extension Center
sources.notes: Freezing injury occurs at -0.6C (30.9F) or lower -- used only to ground the lower temperature bound. No explicit shelf-life duration was found in this research pass; the 7-day figure is a conservative internal estimate reflecting mushrooms' well-known high perishability, not a direct citation. Applied to Jamur Segar.

sources.title: Grape (table grape) produce facts sheet
sources.publisher: UC Davis Postharvest Research and Extension Center
sources.notes: Gray mold (the most destructive postharvest disease of table grapes) develops even at temperatures as low as -0.5C, motivating near-freezing storage. No explicit shelf-life duration was extracted from the fact sheet in this research pass; the 14-day figure is a conservative internal estimate, weaker grounding than the temperature guidance. Applied to Anggur Segar.

sources.title: Strawberry produce facts sheet
sources.publisher: UC Davis Postharvest Research and Extension Center
sources.notes: Store at 0-1C; even under ideal conditions strawberries typically keep only 5-7 days, and delayed cooling beyond 1 hour after harvest reduces marketable fruit. Applied to Stroberi Segar; conservative 5-day end used.

sources.title: Chile Pepper produce facts sheet
sources.publisher: UC Davis Postharvest Research and Extension Center
sources.notes: Best storage at 7.5C for 3-5 weeks; chile peppers (unlike bell peppers) are only mildly chilling-sensitive and can hold at 5C for at least 2 weeks before chilling-injury discoloration appears. Applied to Cabai Segar; conservative 3-week end used for shelf life, 5-7.5C range for ideal temperature.

sources.title: Handling Fresh and Frozen Raw Molluscan Shellfish / state shellfish-handling guidance
sources.publisher: State public health / shellfish sanitation agencies (Rhode Island, Washington State), consistent with FDA's National Shellfish Sanitation Program framework
sources.notes: Live shellfish refrigerated at 35-41F (1.7-5C), stored ventilated (not sealed/submerged). Shelf life 7-10 days for hard-shell clams/oysters but only 3-4 days for mussels -- this dataset uses the shorter mussel-like figure since Indonesian "kerang" commonly refers to mussel-type bivalves (e.g. kerang hijau). Applied to Kerang Segar.

commodity_type.method: Manually selected Indonesian commodity labels for the MVP; which commodities to cover is a product choice, not a literature-derived fact.

temp_ideal_min_c.method: Cross-checked against each commodity's cited public food-safety source; where the source gives a ceiling only (e.g. "40F or below"), the minimum retains its prior ice-storage-practice value since no source specifies a lower bound for unfrozen fresh product. Tomat Segar and Cabai Segar are exceptions, using their chilling-injury thresholds (10C and 5C respectively) instead of a near-0C floor.

temp_ideal_max_c.method: Matched to each commodity's cited maximum safe refrigeration/freezer temperature; Salmon Segar and Tuna Segar were corrected from 2C to 4C on 2026-08-22 to match the FDA fresh-fish ceiling of 40F (4C). Cut-fruit commodities (Mangga/Pepaya/Nanas Potong) use the general FDA fresh-cut-produce ceiling rather than their whole-fruit chilling-injury thresholds. Tomat Segar and Cabai Segar use their chilling-injury-avoidance ceilings (13C and 7.5C), well above every meat/dairy/seafood commodity here.

shelf_life_hours_at_ideal_temp.method: Matched to each commodity's cited storage duration at ideal/safe refrigeration temperature; Salmon Segar and Tuna Segar were corrected from 72h/96h to 48h on 2026-08-22 to match the FDA fresh-fish guidance of 2 days. Sawi Segar uses UC Davis's real 40-day bok choy figure at 0C, materially longer than the other leafy greens -- a genuine postharvest-physiology difference, not an inconsistency. Mangga/Pepaya/Nanas Potong keep the conservative ~48h estimate (no fruit-specific cut-shelf-life citation found). Wortel Segar, Kentang Segar, Jamur Segar, and Anggur Segar's shelf-life figures are internal conservative estimates -- their cited sources ground only a temperature threshold (freezing/chilling injury), not an explicit multi-day duration. Brokoli Segar and Stroberi Segar have direct duration citations (720h and 120h respectively). Used as a relative risk feature, not a food-safety guarantee.

delay_tolerance_hours.method: No public source found (as of this research pass) that defines tolerance to in-transit temperature/time deviation specifically for most commodities; public guidance covers safe storage duration under ideal refrigeration, not cold-chain delay tolerance -- manually defined operational threshold used by the synthetic label function for those. Four exceptions have a direct public citation: Semangka Potong (4h, FDA cut-melon room-temperature-abuse limit), Keju Segar and Yogurt (2h, USDA general dairy room-temperature rule), and Telur Ayam Segar (2h, USDA shell-egg room-temperature rule). The field's overall classification stays DEMO since the current schema has no per-record field override and most commodities still lack any citation. USDA FSIS's general "2-hour rule" (perishable food discarded after 2h at room temperature, 1h above 32C) is a plausible broader anchor for the remaining meat/poultry/seafood commodities not yet applied here -- flagged as a follow-up, not implemented in this pass.

temp_sensitivity_level.method: No public source found (as of this research pass) that categorizes commodities into a Low/Medium/High transport temperature-sensitivity tier. Manually assigned category used by feature engineering.
